rationale: Tests recognition of paraphimosis as a surgical emergency requiring immediate manual reduction
Reinforces that a non-healing penile ulcer must be biopsied and not treated empirically as infection
Tests the optimal timing of orchidopexy and the consequence of delaying treatment beyond age two
Clarifies that orchidopexy reduces the risk of missed tumour by enabling examination, not by eliminating malignancy risk
Tests the priority of excluding torsion in any acutely painful scrotum before assuming epididymo-orchitis
Tests understanding that epididymo-orchitis in young men is commonly sexually transmitted (Chlamydia) requiring GUM referral
Tests knowledge of tumour markers in testicular cancer and the rule that trans-scrotal biopsy is contraindicated
Tests understanding that seminoma is exquisitely radiosensitive whereas non-seminomatous GCTs are treated with BEP chemotherapy
